key_idea: A block that is round from above looks like a rectangle, triangle or circle from the front; a block that is square from above has flat sides.
steps: From above, left to right: red circle, blue square, yellow circle, grey square. From the front the order stays the same.
If the blocks stand up straight, the blue and grey blocks have flat sides, so from the front they look like a square or a rectangle.
The red and yellow blocks are round, so from the front they can look like a rectangle (a can) or a triangle (a cone).
Picture B has red rectangle, blue square, yellow triangle, grey square. That fits.

choice_feedback.A: The blue block is square from above, so if it stands up straight it does not look like a circle from the front.
choice_feedback.C: The order is backwards. From the front the red block is on the left.
choice_feedback.D: The grey block is square from above, so if it stands up straight it does not look like a circle from the front.
choice_feedback.E: The grey block is square from above, so if it stands up straight it does not look like a circle from the front.

review.note: Figure is ambiguous: a cylinder lying on its side with length = diameter looks square from above and round from the front, so A, D and E could also work. B is only the answer if all blocks stand upright. Consider changing the stem or options.
